description:
Execution boundary: planning approved; this issue does not authorize commits, pushes, merges, upstream publication, GitHub comments, live WhatsApp access, or real messages. Revalidate current source/Git state before implementation. Preserve unrelated work, including the already-edited docs/architecture.md. Track this work in the ZAQ Beadwork store even when files belong to the sibling package; do not initialize another store.
Read AGENTS.md in the affected repository. For ZAQ read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md plus the domain policies listed below. Read module documentation before editing. Source navigation uses Serena with bounded fallback if unavailable. Record test results honestly; plan approval is not completed-feature UX approval. Follow repository validation owners; no assertion weakening or unrelated refactors. Existing test changes outside the specifically approved contracts need human approval.

Required domain policies: docs/services/engine.md; docs/services/bo-auth.md; docs/services/channels.md; docs/services/system-config.md for runtime config handling.

Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add:
ZAQ owners: lib/zaq/engine/connector_lifecycle.ex, new lib/zaq/engine/actions/enable_channel_connector.ex, Engine Api explicit :enable_channel_connector handler. Extend lifecycle @moduledoc. Focus on WhatsApp enable journey; do not migrate unrelated provider toggles or silently widen their permission policy.
Provide an explicit enable command, never a toggle. Input exact channel_config_id/provider/kind plus revision/context using existing descriptor conventions. Return ID-only result with status enabled/already_enabled and runtime synced/pending; errors unauthorized/invalid_request/connector_not_found/stale_connector through established conventions. Reject archived connectors. Repeated requests must not disable or create duplicate runtime/profile. Persist through ChannelConfig/changesets at Engine, perform runtime sync outside DB transaction, and coordinate with the exclusion from zaq-e5z.6. Startup failure leaves enabled state with runtime pending; retry converges on the same saved connector.
Confidential Action and current-user revalidation require super_admin, including on execution after context preparation. Nil actor, forged request owner, ordinary admin/staff, revoked/demoted user and nonconfidential event cannot enable or trigger runtime. Reuse BOActor current-user validation; no implicit nil privileges. Jido.Exec.run only at role boundary; BO callers use NodeRouter.
APPROVAL: user explicitly said "okay so this should be fixed to super-admin 4 and 5 are clear now" after the existing non-super-admin enable test and policy difference were explained. Scope is WhatsApp enablement; this authorizes replacing that allowance with rejection, not changing unrelated channel permissions.

Tests to add before implementation:
Add Engine Action/lifecycle tests before implementation: current super-admin success, missing/non-admin/demoted actor and missing confidential context rejection with zero writes/runtime effects, wrong provider/kind, archived/missing/stale connector, repeat enable, concurrent disable/enable, startup failure -> persisted enabled/runtime pending and explicit retry, storage/persistence errors, unchanged unrelated provider behavior. Property cases for malformed scope/revision/actor inputs and idempotence. Use real domain boundaries and isolate external runtime effects.

Branches/paths validated:
Authorized/rejected users, exact scope, stale revision, already enabled, archived, DB failure, startup pending, concurrent cleanup exclusion, retry.

Mocking plan:
Real Action/Jido.Exec/Engine domain, Repo and actor lookup. Mock only external adapter/transport edge using existing opts; no browser-supplied module overrides.

Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content:
Action/module docs plus docs/services/engine.md and channels.md explicit enable permission and runtime-pending behavior; test-approval evidence in this issue.

Action reuse assessment:
Decision: new EnableChannelConnector Action delegating to extended ConnectorLifecycle. DisableChannelConnector covers context/disable/logout, not enable; archive adds destructive archival; direct BO Repo update bypasses service ownership. Reuse descriptor/revision, ChannelConfig mutation and lifecycle runtime sync; do not copy these into the Action. Meaningful composable operation exposed as confidential BO-to-Engine event; no agent/workflow registration. This focused Action issue is the explicit prerequisite for zaq-e5z.8. Verify permission denial and shared lifecycle integration.

comments.text: Enable/disable Actions triggered duplicate execution-boundary code under mix q. Reuse assessment refinement: share only confidential current-super-admin validation and Jido result wrapping in an Engine Actions helper; each Action retains its own allowed operations, and ConnectorLifecycle retains persistence/runtime orchestration. BOActor.current_super_admin reuses current_user for stale identity checks. No agent tool exposure or new business operation.

Implemented explicit Engine EnableChannelConnector Action/event and locked lifecycle enable with in-lock current super-admin revalidation, exact scope/revision/archival checks, ID-only enabled/already_enabled + synced/pending results, and startup retry on saved profile. Shared ConnectorCommand keeps confidential authorization/result wrapping common with disable; BOActor current_super_admin delegates existing identity validator. Validated malformed commands property, actor/privilege/confidential denial, demotion between context/execution, stale/archived/scope failures, pending/retry, real adapter runtime across separate callback Task, stable listener on repeat, concurrent enable waiting through disable then stale rejection. mix q passed; 32 tests + 2 properties passed.
